newsitem.title: USA: Investment in China/HK/Taiwan stocks jumped in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Investment in China/HK/Taiwan stocks jumped in Q3.

text.p: Equity funds with a focus on Asian markets invested most heavily in China, Hong Kong and Taiwan in the third quarter of 1996, according to a Micropal report on Asian regional equity funds.

Overall, the Micropal Emerging Market Fund Monitor survey of 89 portfolios managed by 46 firms found the funds made a third-quarter net investment of about $330 million in the 11 countries represented in the survey.
By comparison, they sold about $425 million of regional stocks during the second quarter.

These funds were net buyers of about $500 million of China/Hong Kong stocks and $180 million of Taiwanese stocks last quarter, Micropal said. They had been net sellers of about $190 million of China/Hong Kong shares and $60 million of Taiwanese shares in the second quarter, it said.
Forty-two of the surveyed firms said China/Hong Kong received their heaviest weighting, up from 40 in the second quarter, the report said.
Of the eight other countries represented, only Singapore and the Philippines also received net inflows in the third quarter, it said.

"Seven of the 11 countries we monitor suffered from net selling pressure, the bulk of which was focused on Thai and Indonesian stocks," said Ian Wilson, editor of Micropal Emerging Market Fund Monitor.
Last quarter, the surveyed funds pulled about $275 million out of the Thai stock market and about $145 million of the Indonesian stock market, Micropal said.
In addition, cash levels fell 20 percent over the quarter to a historically low 2.37 percent, it said.
The funds in the Micropal survey managed about $24.2 billion at the end of the third quarter, Micropal said.
